geo.label: hold / data dependent
parts: Macro Stance

Equities enter the report window under pressure. The S&P 500 closed at 6,798.40, down 1.23% in the prior session and 2.45% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05), while the Nasdaq 100 lost 5.16% over five sessions. Headlines tie the selling to the AI spending debate and the software rout: “Wall Street ends sharply down as AI worries weigh” [[n8136]] and “S&P 500 turns negative for 2026” [[n8135]]. The labour side is softening while factories hold up. Layoffs in January were the highest for a start of year since 2009, according to Challenger [[n7334]], job openings fell to a five-year low in December [[n7342]], yet the January ISM manufacturing index printed 52.6% [[n7197]]. The stance is Mixed: the hard factory data argue against a growth scare, but the labour and earnings-revision signals keep the Fed from leaning toward cuts.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.47% and the 10Y at 4.21% at the prior close, leaving the 10Y−2Y spread at 74 bps and the 10Y−3M spread at 54 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-05). Over 20 observations the 2Y was unchanged (0 bps) and the 10Y rose 6 bps, so the curve is “moderately steep, approaching the long-run average” and the move is “steepening (10Y up, 2Y down/flat)”. Over five observations both tenors fell, the 2Y by 6 bps and the 10Y by 3 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-05). Volatility carried the risk-off message: the VIX rose 16.79% in the prior session and 41.55% over 20 sessions to 21.77, while the dollar index sits at 97.82, up 1.60% over five sessions but down 0.87% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Bond desks are positioning for a steeper curve under the next Fed chair: “Investors ramp up bets on steeper yield curve under Warsh-led Fed” [[n7956]].
New / Most Important

The most important item is the handover at the Fed. Kevin Warsh’s return revives the argument over the Fed’s $6.6 trillion balance-sheet legacy [[n3039]], and Reuters asks whether Warsh “may struggle to lay down new rules of the road for Fed” [[n3200]]. Politico makes the same point about votes: “‘He’ll need to get the votes’: Why Warsh may struggle to get his way at the Fed” [[n7959]]. Senator Tim Scott, “facing block on Fed chair nominee”, said Powell is not a criminal [[n7965]], and Bessent said it would be up to Trump whether to sue his Fed nominee over interest rates [[n8086]]. Powell’s chair term ends in May, according to a headline on Fed ETF positioning [[n3143]]. Governor Lisa Cook wants to “wait and see” on rates [[n7958]] and says inflation progress has stalled [[n7290]].
Playbook ✓

Keep duration short against the long end and hold the steepener while the 10Y is up 6 bps over 20 observations. Buy equity protection through index puts or VIX calls while the VIX stays above its 20-session reference of 15.38 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Reverse the steepener if the January payroll report, now set for Feb. 11 [[n7279]], shows private hiring well above the 22,000 gain the ADP survey recorded [[n7281]]. Equity longs should be cash-generating large caps that fund their own capex; trim software and any name that is still paying for AI growth with debt. Re-risk into the index only on a close back above the 20-session reference of 6,920.93 for the S&P 500.

geo.label: on hold / inflation easing
parts: Macro Stance

The ECB left rates unchanged on February 5 and signalled comfort with the dollar’s weakness [[n2839]], while it “confirms inflation on track” in the Financial Times’ read of the decision [[n2857]]. Euro-area inflation fell to 1.7% in January [[n2796]], the lowest in more than a year on the Bloomberg series [[n2794]]. The stance is Mixed. Inflation is easing toward target, but the ECB’s own survey shows a tightening in bank lending [[n2737]] and euro-zone firms report deteriorating profits [[n2691]], which keeps the bloc’s cyclical recovery narrow.
Credit & Inflation

Bank credit is the weak link. Reuters reports that euro-zone banks are tightening access to business credit according to the ECB survey [[n2739]], and the ECB is widening access to euro loans to boost the currency’s global role [[n2837]]. The EUR/USD closed at 1.18, down 1.47% over five sessions but up 1.07% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The Bank of England’s hold at 3.75% [[n2878]] came on a narrow 5-4 vote [[n2873]], which shows how close the rate decision was across Europe even as the ECB stayed put.
New / Most Important

The European equity story is now a software and AI-disruption story. “FTSE and European firms worst hit by software sell-off” [[n2871]], and RELX and Wolters Kluwer fell on AI competition fears [[n2760]]. European indices had been at a record high on February 4 [[n2813]] and closed lower on the decision day [[n2868]]. German factory orders rose unexpectedly by the most in two years [[n2861]], a data point the market has not yet been willing to pay for. Brussels is also on the agenda: Lagarde will send EU leaders a checklist on strengthening the bloc [[n2841]]. The currency tension is visible too: the ECB’s comfort with dollar weakness [[n2839]] and the pound’s slump after the BoE hold [[n8160]] both show that exchange rates are doing some of the tightening work.
Playbook ✓

Own the euro-area names with buyback capacity; European buybacks reached €182 billion according to Morningstar [[n2869]]. Avoid auto exposure into a weak quarter: Volvo Cars fell over 22% in its worst trading day ever [[n2536]]. Turn Bullish on European banks if the bank-lending survey turns and the STOXX 600 holds above its 20-session reference of 603.83 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Trim the index if the STOXX 600 closes below that level, with the DAX (24,491.06, down 2.53% over 20 sessions) as the confirming signal.

geo.label: targets trimmed / selective support
parts: Macro Stance

Beijing is signalling a smaller growth push. China plans a trimmed GDP growth target that requires less stimulus [[n1085]], and provinces set lower growth targets for 2026 [[n1013]]. The surface data are firmer: the private factory survey shows activity at its fastest pace since October [[n0821]]. The stance is Mixed. Activity is improving at the margin, but the policy anchor is being lowered and the equity tape is not confirming the recovery.
PMIs & Activity

The January private factory PMI accelerated [[n0823]], and services activity picked up with hiring at a six-month high in the survey [[n0955]]. Exporters are expanding: the factory activity gauge for export-oriented firms rose [[n0863]]. The feed carries no numerical official PMI headline, so the view rests on the private surveys and the services and manufacturing headlines above, not on an official print.
Credit Impulse

The feed carries no fresh total social financing or new-loans print. The latest rate signal is the PBOC’s key bank loan rate, which fell to a record low [[n0844]] in a headline dated February 2. Retail demand for equities is picking up, with 4.9 million accounts drawn into the rally in January [[n0971]], and automakers are rolling out longer-term financing plans to spur car demand [[n1015]]. Credit is therefore supporting consumption at the margin rather than the property sector.
Property

Property is still the drag. Shanghai is buying state-owned homes in three districts to halt a market slide [[n1083]] and buying small older flats to revive its ailing housing market [[n0968]]. The sales decline accelerated at the start of 2026 [[n7215]], and developers say the hopeful signs are not real [[n7219]]. Local-government land-sales income fell for a fourth straight year [[n0877]]. This is the part of the economy the tighter growth target has the least room to fix.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Fiscal policy is turning selective. China is raising taxes on select sectors [[n1027]], and the tax worry pushed Hong Kong-listed tech into a bear market alongside AI fears [[n1047]], before the Hong Kong stocks rebounded as the tax concern abated [[n1046]]. Trade is thawing at the edges: China ended its longest boycott of US soybeans, although purchases remain a fraction of prior levels [[n1089]]. On critical minerals, the US proposed a trade bloc to counter China [[n1020]], and Beijing says it opposes “exclusive blocs” [[n1107]].
Markets & Flows

Chinese equities are soft despite the data. The Hang Seng closed at 26,885.24, up 0.14% in the prior session but down 3.87% over five sessions, and the Shanghai Composite closed at 4,075.92, down 0.64% in the prior session and 1.97% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). KWEB closed at 33.37, down 8.05% over five sessions, and the FXI fell 6.33% over five sessions to 38.20. The US-listed CSI 300 ETF (ASHR) closed at 33.20, down 1.57% over 20 sessions. USD/CNY closed at 6.94, down 0.84% over 20 sessions, and the yuan is on a run: “Yuan heads for longest weekly winning streak against dollar in 13 years” [[n1058]].
New / Most Important

The most important item is the EV and tech squeeze. BYD’s $60 billion wipeout “points to deeper turmoil for China EVs” [[n1078]], Brazil scrapped its EV tariff break for BYD [[n1090]], and Canada is scrapping its electric-vehicle rules [[n1091]]. Hong Kong tech is the transmission channel: the tax and AI fears pushed the sector into a bear market [[n1047]], and Nio expects to post its first adjusted operating profit [[n1062]], a sign that some EV names are getting to breakeven even as the sector sells off.
Playbook ✓

Own the yuan carry and the cyclical upturn in the private PMIs at the margin, but do not chase Hong Kong tech into the tax overhang [[n1047]]. Add to Chinese equity exposure only when the Hang Seng holds above its 20-session reference of 26,149 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05) and KWEB stops falling. ⚠ Divergence: the private surveys show expansion while the Shanghai Composite and KWEB are both lower over five sessions, so equity investors are not buying the upturn.

geo.label: hike bias / election risk
parts: Macro Stance

The BOJ is leaning toward a further hike. A board member added to the signals pointing to rate increases [[n3936]], and a policymaker called for a timely hike to manage inflation [[n3937]]. A former currency chief argued that FX intervention should be backed by rate hikes [[n3940]]. The stance is Mixed: the policy direction is hawkish, but the yen is under pressure ahead of the vote and the bond market is being driven by the election rather than the BOJ.
Activity & Currency

USD/JPY closed at 156.92, up 2.50% over five sessions and 0.12% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Reuters polling expects Q4 GDP to return to growth on robust investment [[n3954]]. The Nikkei 225 closed at 53,818.04, down 0.88% in the prior session and up 3.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Corporate earnings are strong: Toyota raised its full-year operating profit outlook by 11.8% [[n3946]], and Sony lifted its outlook after a record quarterly profit [[n3952]]. Japan’s three top banks are on track for record profits [[n3939]]. The yen’s slide is tied to politics as much as to the BOJ, and a Reuters headline already reads the election as the main risk to the bond market.
Playbook ✓

Own the megabanks, which benefit from higher rates as MUFG’s profit rise on BOJ hikes shows [[n3898]], and keep yen exposure hedged rather than short, because intervention risk rises at these levels. Hedge funds have revived yen-weakness trades ahead of the vote [[n3862]], and Trump endorsed Takaichi ahead of Sunday’s election [[n3967]]. Trigger: if the BOJ signals a timely hike [[n3937]] and the yen fails to hold a rebound, add to the banks; if the election is read as fiscal expansion and the JGB curve breaks higher, exit the yen-short and cut long-duration JGB exposure.

geo.label: hiking cycle / household squeeze
parts: Macro Stance

The RBA raised the cash rate to 3.85% after three cuts [[n0174]], its first hike since late 2023 as inflation reached a six-quarter high [[n0173]]. Markets bet on more: HSBC expects one more hike [[n0260]], and the AFR reports that the RBA forecasts materially higher inflation [[n0267]]. The stance is Bearish for domestic demand: the rate path is still rising, and the policy response is being read as a cost-of-living problem rather than a supply fix. WSJ’s read is that the overheating economy signals more rate pain ahead [[n0307]], which makes the hiking cycle a demand question rather than a one-off adjustment.
Demand & Financing

Households are paying the hike. Major Australian banks raised home-loan rates after the central bank’s move [[n7263]], and the banks passed hikes on to mortgage holders but not to savings accounts [[n0337]]. Unions are pushing above-inflation wage increases and threaten strikes [[n0316]], and real wages are not expected to grow until 2027 [[n0318]]. AUD/USD closed at 0.70, down 0.40% in the prior session and up 4.05% over 20 sessions, and the S&P/ASX 200 closed at 8,889.20, up 2.23% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The regulator eased liquidity curbs on Macquarie Bank as risk controls improved [[n3149]], which is the only financing item that moves the other way.
Playbook ✓

Underweight the rate-sensitive domestic names and favour ASX 200 exposure that earns in US dollars or from commodities. The trigger to turn constructive is a wage settlement that falls below the inflation rate, or a banks’ move to pass cuts through to savings rather than only to lending [[n0337]]. Until then, hedge the AUD exposure in any offshore book, because the currency has already risen 4.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).

Tanieją akcje, złoto, srebro oraz kryptowaluty” [[n4637]] (investors take profits; shares, gold, silver and crypto get cheaper), after a record for the Warsaw bourse only the day before [[n4564]].

Keep Polish exposure to the banks that the rate hold favours, and use the WIG20TR tracker rather than single KGHM names until the board turmoil clears. Trigger to add: PKO holding above its 20-session gain, with the Monetary Policy Council’s pause intact. Trigger to cut: a second leg lower in KGHM after the regulator’s review [[n4329]]. ⚠ Divergence: the WIG20TR is still up 4.39% over 20 sessions and the bank index looks strong, while KGH is down 16.59% over five sessions, so the index is leaning on banks that the copper name does not confirm.
Narrative

Tech is the centre of the rout. XLK closed at 135.63, down 7.65% over five sessions and 7.44% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Few seat-based software names are set up for an upside surprise while the sector is being repriced on AI-substitution fears. NextEra closed at 89.21, up 13.83% over 20 sessions, and utilities with large data-centre load are set up to beat on rate-base growth. The surprise is in capex approvals rather than in the quarter, and the feed has no direct utility preview.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The cost of the build-out is becoming political. Axios reports Hawley is circulating a data-centre costs bill [[n6334]], and states are considering new data-centre laws [[n6329]], which cut against a utility rally that depends on those data-centre loads.
Narrative

European autos are being squeezed. The iShares STOXX Europe 600 Automobiles & Parts ETF closed at 45.96, down 3.08% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Volkswagen overtook Tesla as Europe’s top EV seller in 2025 [[n6293]], and the group plans to make the majority of its cars in China by 2030 [[n6296]].
Reported

Volvo Cars shares slumped as the automaker warned of another tough year [[n2535]], and the stock fell over 22% in its worst trading day ever [[n2536]]. Stellantis delayed some EV launches [[n6319]], and Peugeot model launches are delayed by battery plant problems [[n6009]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside is scarce. Volkswagen’s EV position [[n6293]] is the best earnings support in the group, but its 20% pay deal for US workers [[n6300]] is a cost headwind that the EPS model has to absorb. The surprise, if any, comes from EV unit margins rather than volumes.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The EV leader in Europe is a legacy automaker, Volkswagen, not a Chinese maker, which cuts against the consensus that Chinese EVs take over Europe. Xiaomi’s EV push for Europe [[n6295]] is the counter-signal the consensus is ignoring.
Narrative

The AI capex cycle is intact but the group is fragile. SOXX closed at 330.83, down 8.39% over five sessions but up 1.83% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). TSMC is expanding AI chip production to Japan [[n6195]], and the hyperscalers are raising spend [[n6207]]. ASML closed at 1,350.16, up 9.91% over 20 sessions.
Reported

Qualcomm sank 8% on a dire memory-shortage warning [[n6246]]. Arm fell as licensing sales missed estimates [[n2326]]. AMD fell 17% after a dour forecast showed tough competition in AI [[n2349]] and [[n2351]].
EPS Upside Watch

Micron closed at 382.89, up 12.76% over 20 sessions, and is set up for an upside surprise if the memory shortage [[n6246]] keeps pricing firm. SK hynix’s record profits [[n2534]] show the margin is real. ASML’s upside depends on advanced-node capacity, which TSMC’s 3-nanometre plan in Japan [[n6203]] supports.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Chinese memory is the counter-signal. CXMT and YMTC plan to massively expand memory output [[n3875]], and HP, Dell, Acer and Asus are weighing Chinese memory chips amid the supply crunch [[n6244]], which challenges the shortage thesis behind Micron’s rally.

earnings_pattern.title: Beats Are Not Enough: Guidance and Capex Set the Reaction
parts: Rewarded

Reddit rose after its results beat estimates, and it added a $1 billion share buyback [[n2426]][[n2466]]. Roblox shares rocketed on an earnings beat and a strong forecast [[n2424]]. Sony lifted its outlook after a 22% profit jump in the holiday quarter [[n2436]], Rockwell Automation lifted its guidance as profit jumped [[n2438]], and Cardinal Health shares jumped after its earnings [[n2467]]. Elf Beauty lifted its annual forecasts as affordable products drove demand [[n2373]].
Punished

Amazon fell after an earnings miss and a $200 billion capex plan [[n2470]], and the stock fell 8% in the session [[n6225]]. AMD fell 17% after its forecast [[n2349]] and suffered its worst rout since 2018 [[n2375]]. Volvo Cars fell over 22% in its worst trading day ever [[n2536]]. Molina Healthcare sank 28% on a surprise loss [[n2472]], Peloton plunged 26% [[n2461]], and Novo Nordisk fell 17% after a bleak forecast [[n2356]]. Arm fell as licensing sales missed [[n2326]].
Pattern

A beat is not a buy signal. AbbVie beat expectations and the stock fell anyway [[n2316]], and Arm’s fall shows how high the bar is for AI companies now [[n2372]]. Linde beat, and its shares fell as 2026 guidance disappointed [[n2429]]. The second axis is capex: Alphabet’s spending plan overshadowed its results [[n2476]], and Amazon’s cloud beat [[n2483]] did not rescue the shares [[n2470]]. Headlines disagree on how far Alphabet’s stock moved, so this report does not assign it a direction.
Attention into EPS

The next EPS risk is input cost, not demand. Qualcomm warned of a memory shortage [[n6246]], PC makers are qualifying Chinese memory [[n6244]], and Sony overcame a memory crunch to post its profit jump [[n3904]]. SK hynix will pay a record bonus after record profits [[n2534]], so the memory cost cycle is reaching the bonus line of the chip makers.
Playbook

Own the names that raised guidance into any pullback: Reddit [[n2426]], Sony [[n2436]] and Rockwell [[n2438]]. Avoid buying beat-only prints from capex-heavy hyperscalers until the spend line is clear. Trigger to turn Bearish on hardware EPS: a guidance cut from a memory-exposed name such as Qualcomm, which would signal that the shortage is ending [[n6249]].

underowned.title: Indian IT services and the Anthropic tool shock
parts: Attention Gap

Coverage has centred on US software [[n6233]], but Reuters flagged analyst concern that Anthropic’s AI push threatens Indian IT services revenue [[n6237]]. Forbes reported Indian IT stocks were hit hard by fears of the Anthropic tool [[n5948]], and the launch of Opus 4.6 came as another hit to the software market [[n6243]].
Exposure & Risk

The exposure is through listed Indian IT majors and US-listed ADRs of Indian IT services firms, which trade on the same substitution fear as US software. The feed carries no Indian IT price, so this is a read on positioning rather than a measured level. The risk is that a second AI-model release hits seat-based pricing before the sector has reset its guidance. Outsourced testing and maintenance contracts are the work most exposed to an AI tool, so the pricing pressure appears in that revenue line first.
Trigger to Watch

A new AI-model release that is framed as a replacement for outsourced coding or testing work. Watch the next Anthropic release for that framing [[n6232]]. If it arrives and Indian IT revenue commentary turns cautious, the theme becomes consensus.

underowned.title: Private credit and the shadow-bank lenders
parts: Attention Gap

Equity coverage of Blue Owl focuses on the share slump, which Bloomberg describes as a record plunge [[n6290]]. The debt angle is less covered: billions have been wiped off shadow banks as AI threatens a wave of defaults [[n6291]], and the software rout is spreading pain to the debt markets [[n6288]].
Exposure & Risk

The exposure runs through BDC equities and the lenders’ own shares, including Blue Owl. Credit ETFs show a softer tone: HYG closed at 80.53, down 0.62% over five sessions and 0.43% over 20, and LQD at 110.50, down 0.05% over 20. The risk is that a few software-loan marks force a faster repricing than the bond market expects. Blue Owl’s own response matters for the theme: its executive dismissed concerns that AI is disrupting software businesses [[n6289]], and the market is testing that claim.
Trigger to Watch

A software-loan default or a markdown in a BDC’s net asset value. Hedge funds that bet on liquidity over private credit are being paid for it [[n6283]], which suggests the market is already moving toward liquidity. If a markdown lands, the theme becomes consensus quickly.

underowned.title: Data-centre power and the REIT discount
parts: Attention Gap

Utilities get the AI-power headlines, but the discount in property is the under-discussed part. Xcel Energy’s profit rose on AI-driven demand [[n6325]], and data centres are increasingly turning to off-grid gas [[n6338]]. US REITs ended January at a median 16.2% discount to net asset value [[n6345]].
Exposure & Risk

Instruments include XLU, which closed at 43.10 and is up 2.94% over 20 sessions, NextEra at 89.21 (up 13.83% over 20), and data-centre-exposed REITs. Utility cost-recovery risk rises as infrastructure costs and demand both rise [[n6327]]. Political risk is the weak point: state data-centre laws are under consideration [[n6329]].
Trigger to Watch

The Hawley data-centre costs bill [[n6334]]. If it advances, utilities with the largest data-centre load face cost-recovery and rate-design risk, and the REIT discount could narrow if the cost of power for data centres is pushed onto tenants. Refinancing terms for net-lease REITs are open for now, as STORE Capital’s notes sale shows [[n6356]], which means the rate cost is absorbed until a shock closes the window.

underowned.title: Japanese megabanks as the JGB holders
parts: Attention Gap

The headline is record profits: Japan’s three top banks are on track for record profits [[n3939]], and MUFG’s profit rose as BOJ rate increases lifted lending income [[n3898]]. Less covered is the balance-sheet side, as Japan’s biggest banks are ready to increase JGB holdings despite growing losses [[n3938]].
Exposure & Risk

Instruments are the megabank shares, and the Nikkei 225, which closed at 53,818.04 and is up 3.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The risk is that JGB losses offset lending income if the long end sells off around the election [[n3895]].
Trigger to Watch

A BOJ hike that is confirmed in the next meeting, or a sharp JGB yield move after the Sunday election [[n3967]]. A confirmed hike keeps the lending-income story; a bond rout reverses it. Japan’s bank earnings are being reported through a rate cycle that the BOJ is leaning into [[n3937]], so a hike is the cleanest upside trigger for the group.

crypto.title: Crypto: forced selling and a crypto-winter tape
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 62,702.10 on the prior completed daily close, down 14.13% in the prior session and 34.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Ether closed at 1,821.68, down 15.01% in the prior session and 44.72% over 20, and Solana at 78.19, down 15.04% in the session and 46.03% over 20. IBIT closed at 36.10, down 13.16% in the prior session and 29.96% over 20 sessions, and Strategy (MSTR) at 106.99, down 17.12% in the prior session and 33.89% over 20. Bitcoin is back below its level at the start of the Trump second term [[n1452]], and it now trails the S&P 500, the Nasdaq 100 and gold over five years [[n8141]].
New / Most Important

Strategy posted a fourth-quarter loss of $12.4 billion and its shares hit an 18-month low [[n1541]]. The loss headlined the worst crypto day since the 2022 crash [[n1534]]. Bitcoin dropped below $64,000, the lowest since October 2024 [[n1488]], and ETF outflows topped $500 million [[n1487]], with the worst ETF decline in over a year [[n1483]]. Sentiment hit FTX-era lows, with the “extreme fear” reading at 9 [[n1536]].
Playbook

Bearish. Do not buy the first bounce: sell rallies into $70,000 [[n1495]] with a stop above that level, or buy put spreads on MSTR and COIN, which closed at 146.12 after a 40.58% fall over 20 sessions. Trigger to flip: two daily closes back above $70,000 and BTC ETF flows turning positive. Watch the market-structure bill, where talks are picking up after clearing a key vote [[n1508]]. Size any bounce trade small: an ETF outflow streak and a Strategy-driven forced-selling narrative [[n1546]] mean a bounce can fail as quickly as it starts.

flows.title: Capital Flows & Liquidity: the financing squeeze moves into credit
parts: Global Liquidity

Central banks are diverging. The ECB and the Bank of England held rates [[n2839]][[n2873]], the BOJ is leaning toward a hike [[n3936]], and the RBA raised to 3.85% [[n0174]]. The Fed balance sheet is the overhang: Warsh’s return revives tensions over the Fed’s $6.6 trillion QE hangover [[n3039]]. Emerging-market liquidity is the stress test. Indonesia’s $80 billion market rout has prompted draft regulations [[n3136]], and a global watchdog flagged risks in the $16 trillion government-backed repo market [[n3146]]. The liquidity cycle is tightening at the margin rather than easing: Australia reversed course with a rate hike and markets bet on more [[n3853]].
Rates & Dollar

The dollar index closed at 97.82, up 0.20% in the prior session and 1.60% over five sessions but down 0.87% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The curve is “moderately steep, approaching the long-run average”, with 2Y at 3.47% and 10Y at 4.21% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-05). TLT closed at 87.48, down 0.35% over 20 sessions, and IEF at 96.07, down 0.42%. The pound slumped after the BoE hold and the dollar reached a two-week high [[n8160]]. South Korean debt is the most exposed in Asia to a steeper Treasury curve [[n7975]], so the regional transmission is already visible.
Credit Check

Credit is where the AI rout moves into the financing channel: “The Software Rout Is Spreading Pain to the Debt Markets” [[n6288]], and Blue Owl’s shares extended a record plunge [[n6290]]. HYG closed at 80.53, down 0.62% over five sessions. Oracle’s $25 billion bond sale eased fears of an AI debt wave [[n3034]], but Oracle plans to raise up to $50 billion in debt and equity [[n3035]], so the credit check is not finished. Private-credit lenders with the most software exposure are the ones being repriced first [[n6291]], and that is where the credit check will fail if it fails.
Equity & Fund Flows

Money is leaving US tech without leaving the asset class. Global ex-US equity funds drew inflows as investors shunned pricey US tech [[n8113]], and ETF demand in January set record inflows [[n3128]]. Hedge funds were hit by the AI sell-off [[n3179]], and they are saying no to new cash just as clients rush to allocate [[n3220]]. Buybacks remain the domestic support: Reddit’s $1 billion repurchase [[n4873]], and European buybacks of €182 billion [[n2869]]. Capital is also moving to new hubs: Dubai’s financial centre reports a hedge-fund boom [[n3163]] while US hedge funds sell down AI-exposed names.
Portfolio Implication

Keep gross exposure modest until the January payroll data [[n7279]] is in, and fund the position from buyback-supported large caps rather than from AI-capex-heavy names. Use HYG as the credit gauge: a close below its 20-session reference of 80.88 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05) confirms that the credit channel is tightening, and the portfolio should then cut cyclical credit risk first. Size the cash line for a data gap, because the calendar has already slipped once when a partial shutdown delayed the jobs report [[n7208]].

anticipatory.title: January payrolls on Feb. 11: the labour test for the steepener
parts: What Is Priced

The January jobs report was rescheduled to Feb. 11 after the shutdown delay [[n7279]]. Private payrolls rose by only 22,000 [[n7281]], Challenger counted the highest January layoffs since 2009 [[n7334]], and December job openings were at a five-year low [[n7342]]. Bond desks are already leaning to a steeper curve [[n7956]].
Conditional Expression

If payrolls are weak, express it as a 2s10s steepener: long 2Y against short 10Y, with the curve at 74 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-05), and buy protection on the Russell 2000, which closed at 2,577.65 after a 1.79% fall in the prior session. If payrolls are strong, the curve bear-flattens and rate-sensitive small caps underperform, so cut the steepener and keep the equity hedge.
Risk

The report is itself a noisy event after the shutdown delay, and the ISM services print at 53.8% [[n7272]] runs against the weak payroll signals. A strong ISM with weak payrolls would argue for a smaller position than the curve trade implies. The Fed’s own voice matters too: Governor Cook wants to wait and see on rates [[n7958]], so a weak print will not automatically bring a cut.

anticipatory.title: Warsh confirmation and the Fed balance-sheet question
parts: What Is Priced

Warsh’s nomination revived concern over the Fed’s $6.6 trillion QE legacy [[n3039]], and WSJ notes that saying you want to shrink the Fed is one thing and doing it is another [[n3037]]. Senator Scott’s hold on the nominee [[n7965]] and Bessent’s comment that Trump would decide whether to investigate Warsh over his refusal to cut rates [[n8067]] make the timetable uncertain.
Conditional Expression

If Warsh is confirmed on schedule, the market prices a faster balance-sheet run-down and a steeper curve: the trade is the 2s10s steepener and a short in the metals debasement trade, which Reuters said crashed precious metals on the Warsh specter [[n3043]]. If the nomination stalls, the steepener loses its anchor: cut the trade and hold GLD at 441.88, up 7.98% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).
Risk

The Fed is not a single vote: Politico argues that Warsh may have to win the votes to get his way [[n7959]], and Fortune noted that Powell could stay on while Miran resigns [[n7967]]. The board dynamics can differ from the nominee’s stated views, which is the main risk to a clean steepener. Politico’s view is that the Trump pick may surprise him [[n7972]], which means the policy path could diverge from the nominee’s public line.

anticipatory.title: Japan’s Sunday election and the yen-JGB link
parts: What Is Priced

Trump endorsed Takaichi ahead of Sunday’s election [[n3967]], and hedge funds revived yen-weakness trades ahead of the vote [[n3862]]. The BOJ has said it will not come to the rescue of a Takaichi-driven bond rout [[n3895]], and USD/JPY closed at 156.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05).
Conditional Expression

A decisive win is, in Reuters’ framing, the best scenario for bonds and the yen [[n3941]]. If the result is clear, hold megabank exposure [[n3939]] and keep yen shorts only with an intervention stop. If the result is hung, the yen rallies on the BOJ hike path and the megabanks give back their 20-session gains. Crypto is a live channel too: a bitcoin slide below $64,000 would deepen ETF outflows that have already turned negative [[n1488]].
Risk

Intervention is the main risk: a former currency chief argued FX intervention should be backed by rate hikes [[n3940]], and Japan’s finance bureaucrats were scrambling after the PM’s idle yen comments [[n3861]]. A yen rally from intervention would reverse the short with no change in the BOJ path.

anticipatory.title: US–Iran talks on Friday and the oil premium
parts: What Is Priced

The US and Iran agreed to Friday talks in Oman but remain at odds over the agenda [[n3501]], and the US asked American citizens to leave Iran now ahead of the talks [[n3581]]. Oil already fell: Brent closed at 67.55, down 2.75% in the prior session and up 12.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05), and oil settled almost 3% lower on easing supply concerns [[n6250]].
Conditional Expression

If the talks progress, the geopolitical bid comes out of crude: trim XLE and Exxon (146.08, up 23.28% over 20 sessions) into strength, and reduce the USO position (76.69). If the talks fail, buy calls on USO, which is up 13.13% over 20 sessions, and hold the energy group as the hedge.
Risk

The military tail is real. The US shot down an Iranian drone approaching an aircraft carrier [[n3527]], and Trump warned Iran’s supreme leader should be “very worried” [[n3580]]. A sudden escalation would move Brent faster than the talks can price a deal. If a deal is struck, the risk to the oil bid is a reversal in the 20-session gain that Brent has already put on, so the trade is a fade of the premium rather than a bet on a supply shock.

catalysts.title: $GOOGL — capex-led AI leader
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Alphabet beat estimates on earnings and revenue [[n2315]], and Reuters says Google has gone from laggard to leader as it pulls ahead of OpenAI on AI growth [[n6215]]. The catalyst is the 2026 spend plan of $180 billion [[n6217]], which the market must underwrite with cloud revenue. The thesis is that the spend funds a growing share of AI cloud demand. Alphabet also reported that its cloud business is booming [[n5929]], which is the revenue line that has to justify the spending.
Price Hurdle & Risk

GOOGL closed at 331.25, down 0.54% in the prior session and 2.07% over five sessions, but up 2.88% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Headlines disagree on how the stock reacted to the report [[n2423]][[n2425]], so the hurdle is the capex number rather than the beat.
Trade Expression

Buy the shares or a three-month call spread on pullbacks. The position is invalidated if the capex guidance rises again without matching cloud revenue growth, or if the search franchise shows a visible slowdown. Size the position so that a single-session shock on a capex headline is affordable.

catalysts.title: $TSM — Japan capacity for the AI cycle
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

TSMC’s CEO flagged 3-nanometre chip production in Japan, with the investment reported at $17 billion [[n6203]], and TSMC will make advanced AI chips at its second Japan plant [[n3959]]. The thesis is that the Japan build-out diversifies advanced-node capacity and keeps the AI chip supply chain with the leader. Bloomberg framed the Japan upgrade as a win for Takaichi [[n3924]], which adds a political tailwind to the capacity story.
Price Hurdle & Risk

TSM closed at 330.73, up 1.53% in the prior session and 3.78% over 20 sessions, though down 2.60% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The risk is that the SOXX group, which closed at 330.83 and is down 8.39% over five sessions, keeps de-rating on memory and AI-substitution fears.
Trade Expression

Long TSM against SOXX, sized so that the pair is market-neutral on the AI theme. The trade is invalidated if the Japan plant timetable slips or if the group’s memory-cost squeeze spreads into foundry pricing.

catalysts.title: $MU — memory tightness with a China overhang
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Qualcomm sank 8% on a dire memory-shortage warning [[n6246]], and HP, Dell, Acer and Asus are considering Chinese memory chips amid the supply crunch [[n3958]]. The thesis is that tight memory supply keeps pricing firm into the next quarter, and Micron is the cleanest US exposure. Sony also cited a memory crunch in its profit jump [[n3904]], which says the cost pressure is across hardware, not only in one company.
Price Hurdle & Risk

MU closed at 382.89, up 0.92% in the prior session and 12.76% over 20 sessions, but down 12.14% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The overhang is China: CXMT and YMTC plan to massively expand memory output [[n3875]].
Trade Expression

Buy shares on the five-session weakness, with a stop below the 20-session reference close of 339.55 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The position is invalidated if Chinese memory output expansion is confirmed in pricing data.

catalysts.title: $AMZN — the capex shock and the AWS offset
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Amazon shares fell on an earnings miss and a $200 billion capex plan for 2026 [[n2470]], and Amazon’s cloud unit beat on revenue and profit [[n2483]]. About 80% of the capex is AI-related [[n6216]]. The thesis is that AWS growth pays for the spend, but the market is waiting for the margin evidence. The stock’s reaction is a test of whether investors will keep paying for the AI cycle, since the spending plan is the largest in the group [[n6219]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

AMZN closed at 222.69, down 4.42% in the prior session and 7.81% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). Amazon’s advertising business grew 22% over the past year [[n2523]], which is the cushion the price has not yet priced in. Amazon’s grocery push is also a retail-share question against Walmart [[n2386]], which adds a second front to the margin debate.
Trade Expression
Hold shares, and buy a put spread only if the capex guide rises again. The position is invalidated if the next quarter shows AWS margin expansion that offsets the capex line.

catalysts.title: $ORCL — debt-funded AI build
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Oracle sold a $25 billion bond to ease fears of an AI debt wave [[n3034]] and plans to raise up to $50 billion in debt and equity this year [[n3035]]. It also suffered its worst eight-day stretch in over two decades [[n3197]]. The thesis is that funding needs outrun the equity’s capacity to absorb dilution. MarketWatch frames the bond sale as a sign of anxiety about AI funding [[n3101]], so the credit market is already pricing the financing gap.
Price Hurdle & Risk

ORCL closed at 136.48, down 6.95% in the prior session, 19.25% over five sessions and 29.23% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The hurdle is the next funding deal: a structure that cuts dilution would remove the bear case quickly.
Trade Expression
Bear put spread into the next funding headline, or short the shares against a long on the credit leg. The trade is invalidated by a funding structure that avoids new equity and a bond rally.

catalysts.title: $MSTR — the bitcoin treasury stress
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Strategy posted a $12.4 billion fourth-quarter loss, and its shares hit an 18-month low [[n1541]]. It holds 713,502 BTC [[n1557]], and a headline warns that its bitcoin losses could be catastrophic if bitcoin falls to $60,000 [[n1545]]. The thesis is forced-selling and funding risk for a treasury company whose stock is trading as a levered bitcoin. The worst-drawdown framing is already in the headlines: bitcoin is heading toward the worst drawdown since the FTX crash [[n1530]].
Price Hurdle & Risk
MSTR closed at 106.99, down 17.12% in the prior session and 33.89% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The invalidation level is BTC back above $70,000 [[n1495]].
Trade Expression

Short the shares or buy puts against the bitcoin rally. The position is invalidated by BTC closing back above $70,000 [[n1495]] on two daily closes and by a funding announcement that removes the forced-selling risk.

retail.title: Reddit / RDDT — the buyback and the AI-ad story
parts: Observed Attention

Reddit shares rose on strong guidance and a $1 billion buyback [[n2426]], and Reuters reports strong revenue as AI tools drive ad sales [[n4867]]. Traders were checking the stock before the report [[n4805]], and Stocktwits-style attention centred on its humans-first positioning [[n4868]].
Motivation & Bias
The bias is toward the buyback and the AI-ad story, not the ad-cycle risk. The stock’s appeal is that it is a platform with a real user base in a market that is selling AI-exposed names [[n6233]].
Instrument & Risk

Shares or short-dated calls. The risk is gap risk after a post-earnings move, and Barron’s reports that the shares gained after results beat estimates [[n2466]], so the reaction is already in the price.

retail.title: Figma / FIG — down 40% and called a steal
parts: Observed Attention

Stocktwits reports Figma is down over 40% this year, and retail traders feel it is a steal now [[n4851]]. The attention is in the software-selloff tape, where the sector lost nearly $1 trillion in seven days [[n6233]].
Motivation & Bias

Mean reversion after a broad software rout. Retail reads the software selloff as indiscriminate, which is the bias to test: the same AI-substitution argument that drove the sector down still applies to design tools.
Instrument & Risk
Shares or a small call position sized for a 40% drawdown. The risk is that the software derating continues as Anthropic’s upgrade tools [[n6232]] widen the substitution fear.

retail.title: iShares Silver Trust / SLV — retail won’t let go
parts: Observed Attention

Retail traders aren’t giving up on SLV even after silver’s plunge [[n4780]]. SLV closed at 66.69, down 15.77% in the prior session and 36.83% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The attention is on dip-buying in precious metals, which Bloomberg compares to a meme stock [[n4815]].
Motivation & Bias

The bias is to buy the dip in a market where the trend has been down for a week. Retail is treating the metals rout as a discount, which is the risk this story carries. Bloomberg’s headline on the mood is that fans “hate this new volatility” but keep the faith [[n4806]].
Instrument & Risk

SLV or silver futures. Silver closed at 76.53 and fell 32.89% over five sessions, so position size should reflect that volatility. Silver fell 11% in the morning session per Forbes [[n6451]], which is the risk the dip buyers are taking.

retail.title: Coinbase / COIN — the exchange as a crypto proxy
parts: Observed Attention

Cathie Wood loaded up on Coinbase, Circle and Robinhood as the crypto market was gripped by extreme fear [[n1492]]. Fortune reports that shares in Coinbase and Circle tumbled as the crypto market fell [[n1528]]. Retail sentiment is weak across the speculative tier too: XRP led crypto losses as Ethereum and Dogecoin cratered [[n1479]].
Motivation & Bias
Retail treats the exchange as a discounted way to own the crypto recovery. The bias is that a recovery in volume will return, while the crypto-winter reading argues the volume is still falling.
Instrument & Risk

COIN closed at 146.12, down 13.34% in the prior session and 40.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-05). The risk is correlation to bitcoin, which closed at 62,702.10, so a COIN long is a levered bitcoin call with an equity overlay.
